utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Mister Registrar, would you please call the case. Or Madam Registrar, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case IT-05-87-A, the Prosecutor versus Sainovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I now have the appearances of the parties. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CROSS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution, my name is Matthew Cross, together with Ms. Laurel Baig and our Case Manager is Mr. Colin Nawrot. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now for the Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm Toma Fila appearing for the accused Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. My name is Tomislav Visnjic. Myself and Russell Hopkins appearing for General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm John Ackerman, along with Aleksandar Aleksic. We're appearing for General Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Counsel Mihajlo Bakrac for Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Co-Counsel Dan Ivetic appearing on behalf of Sretan Lukic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have difficulties to see you. Thank you. Before we start, could we call the parties to see whether they could hear the proceedings in a language that they understand. Mr. Sainovic. THE APPELLANT SAINOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ojdanic. THE APPELLANT OJDANIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pavkovic. THE APPELLANT PAVKOVIC: [Interpretation] I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic. THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC: [Interpretation] I can hear in a language I understand, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic. THE APPELLANT LUKIC: [Interpretation] I can follow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. This Status Conference is called in accordance with the Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal which requires a Status Conference to be convened every 120 days during the appeal proceedings to allow that any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation hereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on the 16th May, 2012. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order issued on the 13th August 2012. First, I would like to inquire into the status of the detention conditions and the health situation of the Appellants. If you have any concern in relation to the detention condition or your state of health that cannot be resolved through the standard procedures, I would invite you to raise them now. If you wish, this discussion can take place in private session. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, you have the floor, please. THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC: [Interpretation] Mr. President, here I am again, and to begin with, I would like to thank you most cordially for giving me the floor again. I feel the need, and the duty as well, to acquaint you, with your leave, with my health situation over the past four years through two brief pieces of information.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Four months, correction. THE APPELLANT LAZAREVIC: [Interpretation] First of all, at the last Status Conference on 16 May, I informed you that a council of medical experts will be arriving in keeping with the decision of the Government of Serbia so that you could gain full insight into my health status. This three-member medical panel was here in The Hague from 13 to 15 June this year. They performed clinical examinations, to the best of their ability, and acquainted themselves with the details of all my medical documentation for the past six, seven years. Concluding the examination, this panel notified some of their conclusions pending a detailed report that would be first submitted to the Government of Serbia. Their basic conclusions, Mr. President, are briefly as follows: One, a large number of surgeries - seven in the past three years to be specific - have considerably affected my health overall, both in terms of my mental and physical status after the trial Judgement. The second conclusion. As they say, they established without any doubt that my current health status and my condition require urgent new laboratory tests and diagnostic procedures, the methods of which are difficult to pronounce but it involves multi-slide scanners, colonoscopies, and all the other procedures that they will list in detail, and that have not yet been applied in my case here in The Hague. Their third conclusion is this: They say that my health has considerably deteriorated. It is degraded overall, especially my digestive system, my neurological problems, psychiatric problems, vascular and oral conditions. And the fourth conclusion - the way I listed it for my purposes - is that, based on the examinations they performed, they see symptoms of a chemical affliction of the brain with ischemic infarctions of the brain and a reduced density of the brain mass. I must note that this conclusion made by experts is diametrically opposite to all the findings of the general practitioners from the Detention Unit that have been informing this Court so far about neurological problems. They say that there is a constant anxiety/depressive disorder in my case, resulting from the overall stressful situation of the past years. These would be briefly their conclusions. I have also been informed by my Defence team that the complete report of these experts is already before the Government of the Republic of Serbia, and not later than tomorrow, on Thursday, the Government of Serbia will make its decision on the report, and then forward it to the Tribunal and all those who need to receive it. Upon receipt of this report, my Defence team will approach the competent authorities to arrange the necessary diagnostic and medical and other procedures to repair my health in the short time. The second point is this: Mr. President, also, at the last Status Conference I informed you about my oral health, and following your instructions, I approached the Registry of the Tribunal with a request for assistance. This correspondence between the Registrar and the Deputy Registrar, on the one hand, and myself has been going on for four months over which period we have had a few direct contacts, all for the purpose of addressing my health problems. Specifically, the absence of any teeth in my upper jaw and my inability to use a mobile denture, mobile dentures, since February 2009. This problem also complicates my digestive problems and my overall health situation. In these four months, based with conversations with the dentist from the DU, the Registry came up with two positions. One, I quote: "There is no medical justification for any different type of treatment, including implants." This position of the Registry is, to say the least, debatable. The second position of the Registry was put in writing. It addresses the issue of why I have been deprived of the necessary medical treatment in the past. They explain that this type of intervention is extremely expensive because it is a very new procedure. Concerning this second position, I know that the Registry is trying with the Defence Ministry of the Netherlands to find some sort of solution to provide me with the necessary implants that my condition requires according to the opinion of dental surgeons as well. As for my Defence, we have requested from the Government of the Republic of Serbia an expert report on the first position of the Registry. In other words, we asked for an expert explanation why there would be no medical justification for a procedure which is widely used throughout the world. My Defence team and I are not asking for anything special, such as pearl implants, or heat-resistant implants. Second, we have asked which medical institution in Serbia and under what circumstances would be able to provide me with this surgery. This is all I would have to say today. I thank you again for giving me the floor. Thank you for your patience and your confidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lazarevic. You may sit down, please. Mr. Lazarevic, first of all I would like to thank you very much for informing me about your health conditions at this moment, and we are expecting the reports sent by the Serbia government pretty soon as you mentioned. After that, we will see what kind of action could the Tribunal take. As for your second issue, I believe that we are not in the position to judge whether your medical care is justified or not. We will leave this entirely in the hands of the experts and the dentists. But, anyway, I'll convey your complaint to the Registrar. And also, at the same time, I would like to remind you that, according to the detention rules, if you have any complaints, you could do that according to the normal procedure. Thank you. Is there any other issues that Defence would like to raise? I see none. So before we turn to any other issues that parties may wish to raise, I would like to note that there are currently no pending motions in the present case. At this point, I also would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise. Is there any issue the Prosecution would like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CROSS
utterances.text: We have nothing to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And counsel for Mr. Sainovic, do you have any other issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And counsel for Mr. Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: We have nothing to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Nothing at this time, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have nothing at this time, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I believe this concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance and I'll adjourn these proceedings.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
